question.knowledge_point: Computing a Trigonometric Ratio Using the Pythagorean Identity
question.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13931905/assets/5d292a3598346bd05511c9c8979ba42845a88afe75a4740d8c4bdb9aa3968c87.png)

The diagram above shows the unit circle. Given that the $x$-coordinate of the point $P$ is $\frac{5}{9},$ use the Pythagorean identity to find $sin⁡\theta .$
question.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13931905/assets/488ff32187c9a9a335e3782fb717242d899f622c43010662e28edcabe0e1bde3.png)

Any point $(x,y)$ on the unit circle is related to the central angle $\theta $ as follows:

$$
x=cos⁡\theta ,\,y=sin⁡\theta 
$$

We're given that $x=\frac{5}{9}$ at the point $P.$ Therefore, we have

$$
cos⁡\theta =\frac{5}{9}.
$$

We can use the Pythagorean identity to find $sin⁡\theta :$

$$
\begin{aligned}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta +{cos}^{2}⁡\theta  & =1 \\ {sin}^{2}⁡\theta  & =1-{cos}^{2}⁡\theta  \\ sin⁡\theta  & =\pm \sqrt{1-{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $cos⁡\theta =\frac{5}{9}$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}sin⁡\theta  & =\pm \sqrt{1-{(\frac{5}{9})}^{2}} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{1-\frac{25}{81}} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{\frac{56}{81}} \\  & =\pm \frac{2\sqrt{14}}{9}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we select the positive answer since $sin⁡\theta $ is positive in the first quadrant. So our final answer is $sin⁡\theta =\frac{2\sqrt{14}}{9}.$
